article_title.ru: Общие координаты сил помогают кисти робота отделять предметы
article_title.en: A shared force frame improves a robot hand's removal tasks
article_title.ja: 指先の力を共通座標へ変換し、はがす作業の成功率を改善

caption.ru: В исследовании команды Йоркского университета и партнёров силы трёх пальцев роботизированной кисти приводят к общей системе координат у запястья. Условная редакционная сцена стендового опыта: инженер работает за компьютером, а камеры наблюдают отделение приклеенного образца. Форма образца и компоновка стенда обобщены.
caption.en: In the University of York team and partners’ study, forces from three robotic fingers are expressed in a shared coordinate frame at the wrist. This conceptual editorial scene shows an engineer operating a computer as cameras observe an adhered sample being detached. The sample shape and bench layout are generalized.
caption.ja: ヨーク大学などの研究では、ロボットハンドの三本の指で測った力を、手首を基準にした共通の座標で表す。技術者がコンピューターを操作し、カメラが接着した試料をはがす様子を捉える、研究台での試験を題材にした編集イラスト。試料の形と装置の配置は一般化して描いた。

alt.ru: Чёрно-белая гравюра: женщина-инженер восточноазиатской внешности сидит за ноутбуком и печатает. Обе её ноги и ступни видны и опираются на пол. На столе трёхпалая роботизированная кисть закреплена на каретке вертикальной направляющей. Боковые пальцы охватывают небольшой прямоугольный образец над опорной пластиной, третий палец расположен сзади; у края образца виден тонкий слой приклеивания. Три камеры на устойчивых стойках направлены на этот участок. Экран ноутбука обращён от зрителя; надписей и логотипов нет.
alt.en: Black-and-white engraving of an East Asian woman engineer typing at a laptop, with both legs and feet visible and supported on the floor. A three-finger robotic hand is mounted on the carriage of a vertical guide on the bench. Its side fingers grip a small rectangular sample over a supported plate, with the third finger behind it and a thin adhesive layer visible at the sample’s edge. Three cameras on stable posts face the same contact area. The laptop screen faces away from the viewer; there are no words or logos.
alt.ja: 白黒の版画。東アジア系の女性技術者がノートパソコンを操作し、両脚と床に着いた両足が見える。研究台では三本指のロボットハンドが縦方向の移動装置に固定されている。左右の指が支持板の上の小さな長方形の試料を挟み、三本目の指は奥にある。試料の端には薄い接着層が見える。安定した支柱に取り付けた三台のカメラが同じ接触部分へ向く。パソコンの画面は奥を向き、文字やロゴはない。

visual_thesis: Одна статья dexremo-force-frame: измерения силы на сгибающихся пальцах нужно описывать в общих координатах, чтобы сопоставлять контактные сигналы. Показывается локальный опыт отделения приклеенного образца, а не мобильная автономная система. Фиксированная ориентация запястья и вертикальная направляющая сохраняют ограничения JSON. Персонаж и форма образца условны; не заявляется документальное изображение авторов или точная конструкция DexRemo.
visual_brief:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create exactly ONE original landscape newspaper editorial illustration. Black ink on absolutely pure white, mid-20th-century Soviet popular-science engraving language, strong confident contours, expressive solid black shapes, disciplined sparse hatching and crosshatching, light faces and hands, ample white space. Contemporary robotics. No color, sepia, gray paper, wash, neon, border, logos, captions, letters, numbers, graphs or fake user interfaces. Do not copy any existing figure or make a collage.

ONE coherent scene, based on the November 15 engineering article about a three-finger force-sensing robotic hand for removing adhered objects. This is a generalized editorial concept, not reportage or an exact drawing of DexRemo. Do not add invented performance data or claim a fully mobile autonomous robot.

On a clean, structurally supported laboratory bench, show a small THREE-finger research hand suspended palm-down from a rigid wrist carriage on a single vertical linear guide. Its wrist orientation is fixed; its support and guide connect continuously to a stable broad base on the bench. No robot arm. Minimal plausible geometry: a compact palm with exactly three articulated fingers, two curving inward from opposite sides and the third clearly behind them. Small simple fingertip force-sensing pads integrated into the fingertips, not decorative extra parts. Three fingers grasp the SAME small rectangular solid test block. Two opposing pads visibly press the two opposite VERTICAL side faces of the block. The third finger contacts its rear side without merging with the other two. Fingers do not pierce the block or the bench. All three fingers connect mechanically through visible joints to the palm.

The block is being lifted and slightly tilted to detach it from a broad flat specimen plate resting squarely on the bench. Show an unambiguous small opening under the lifted near edge of the block, with its far bottom edge still bonded to a small remaining adhesive patch on the plate. Side view in a slightly elevated front three-quarter perspective makes the opposing fingertip contacts, lifted edge, residual attachment and plate support readable. The block is not floating: grasp pads support it, the remaining bond anchors one edge, the plate rests on the bench. No debris, cup handles, extra tools or unrelated test objects. The vertical guide is the source of upward motion; its carriage, wrist, fingers, block and supported plate form one visually continuous causal chain. Do not show motion arrows.

Exactly ONE adult East Asian woman engineer, attractive harmonious realistic face and proportions, focused and dignified, in a plain professional work jacket and trousers with closed shoes, seated to the side at a compact computer. Visible specific action: both hands operating the keyboard while she watches the hand's contact with the specimen, collecting the trial through the computer. Her laptop is on the same supported bench away from the moving hand; show only its back and edge so there is NO visible screen content, text or pseudo-interface. Her face and hands stay light, her wrists meet the keyboard naturally. Show her WHOLE BODY, two connected legs from seated hips through bent knees to TWO shoes resting on the floor, with no cropping or furniture hiding her lower legs. Chair seat supports her pelvis and has a stable base. No romantic pose, no hand supporting chin, no gazing at viewer.

Three small plain cameras on simple firmly attached bench posts face the SAME contact region, placed out of the working envelope. Keep their sightlines clear and their mounting mechanically plausible; their purpose is observation, not decoration. Cable routing is minimal, along the support and behind the bench, never through a person or solid object.

Minimal slightly futuristic laboratory furniture: thin smooth rounded tabletop, slim structural outer supports with stable feet, open legroom. Background mostly blank white. No wall poster because no historical insert is necessary to explain the experiment. Research hand and block contact are the clear visual focus; human figure supports the scene without obscuring the mechanics. Nothing else in the room.

Before rendering, simplify any nonessential detail. Verify: exactly three mechanically connected robot fingers, opposed contacts on the same block, continuous guide-to-wrist support, block edge adhesion and lift physically possible, specimen plate supported, human has two complete legs and feet on floor, both hands act on keyboard, exactly three supported cameras directed at the one experiment. A clear original single scene that survives reduction and monochrome newspaper printing. Landscape about 3:2.

Targeted mechanical revision:
Edit this image with ONE targeted mechanical clarification; preserve the woman engineer, full two legs and shoes, her keyboard work, all three cameras, bench, three-finger hand and vertical guide, the engraving style and composition. Correct ONLY the sample and its adhesive contact. The rectangular test piece should be a LOW thick rectangular block, not a nearly vertical thin card. It is tilted only about 10 degrees from lying flat. The near bottom edge is slightly raised, with a clear small white air gap beneath it. The far bottom edge REMAINS CONNECTED by a thin dark adhesive seam to the horizontal specimen plate: draw the continuous physical attachment clearly. Remove the loose white blob beside the block entirely. Two opposed robot fingertip pads press the left and right vertical SIDE FACES of the same block, neither touching air nor passing through it. Third rear fingertip remains visibly connected to the palm and braces its rear side. Show all three fingers, no extra fingers. Grasp and the small remaining adhesive seam support the block; the plate rests flat on the bench. Preserve clear negative space and no text or UI. The chain vertical guide → wrist → fingers → gripped block → remaining attached far edge → supported plate must be visually unambiguous. Do not alter any other object or add decoration. Original black ink on pure white, disciplined sparse hatching. Keep every human foot comfortably inside frame.
